answer: A beacon registry resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before its identity is listed, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real capital. Peers audit the registry like a lantern held over the ledger, flagging identities whose behavior diverges from their stake. Identities that pass repeated audits earn a relic status, a durable non-transferable reputation token that unlocks higher-value work. Forging that history would cost more than any single scam could earn, so honest participation becomes the cheaper strategy.
